newsitem.title: HONG KONG: APP Global Finance launches US$500 mln FRN.
newsitem.headline: APP Global Finance launches US$500 mln FRN.

text.p: Union Bank of Switzerland has launched for APP Global Finance a five-year US$500 million floating rate note issue.
Proceeds of the issue ultimately will be used by Asia Pulp and Paper, but that company has no ownership interest, either directly or indirectly, in issuer APP Global Finance.
Terms and conditions of the transaction and an explanation of its structure follow:
BORROWER APP GLOBAL FINANCE LTD
AMT US$500 MLN COUPON 6ML+400 MATURITY 5 YRS
TYPE FRN ISS PRICE PAR RE-OFFER 99.625
PUTS NONE CALLS NONE REPLIES 20.SEP.96
LISTING LUXEMBOURG REPAYMENT BULLET DENOMS US$100K
RATINGS NONE SALE LMTS CUSTOMARY
NEG PLG NO CRS DEF YES FORCE MAJ YES
GOV LAW NEW YORK HOME CTRY INDONESIA TAX PROV NA
PAY DATE 04.OCT.96 TENTATIVE
MGT LEVELS AND FEES LEADS US$30 MLN 175 BP ALL-IN 435
CO-LEAD US$15 MLN 125 BP ALL-IN 425
CO-MGRS US$5 MLN 75 BP ALL-IN 415
CO-MGRS US$3 MLN 50 BP ALL-IN 410
ARRANGER UBS SINGAPORE
APP Global Finance Ltd is a limited liability wholly owned special purpose finance subsidiary of APP Global Ltd, the controlling shareholder of Asia Pulp & Paper Co.

Global currently holds 86.2 percent of the issued ordinary shares of APP. APP does not own, directly or indirectly, any interest in the issuer and neither the issuer nor Global is a member of the APP Group.
The primary purpose of the issuer is to issue the notes and to invest in and hold redeemable preference shares issued by Finance (I), a wholly owned subsidiary of APP Ltd.
The notes will be secured by a pledge by Global of 50.1 percent of the outstanding voting stock of APP and a pledge by Finance (1) as the issuer of the redeemable preference shares.
Neither Global, APP nor any other entity or person guarantees the notes.
The issuer will use proceeds of the note to subscribe for the redeemable preference shares offered by Finance (1) at a par value of US$100,000 per share.

Finance (1) will use the proceeds of the sale of redeemable preference shares to subscribe from Asia Pulp & Paper Ltd a floating rate note due 2001 (the APP note) in a principal amount equal to the principal amount of the APP Global Finance note.

The issuer expects the interest and principal payments on the APP note to serve as a source of funding for Finance (1) to make dividend and redemption payments under the redeemable preference shares, which in turn will be a source of funding for the issuer to make interest, principle and redemption payments on the notes.
